claimPolicy.verifiedSignature: A signature was independently checked against its public key and exact challenge bytes.
claimPolicy.thresholdCryptography: A threshold or aggregate cryptographic construction executes in code and tests.
claimPolicy.decentralizedCustody: Signing shares or keys are controlled by independently administered failure and authorization domains.
claimPolicy.productionQualified: Runtime, custody, ceremony, recovery, review, monitoring, and release evidence all pass policy.

systems.reason: Three P-256 KMS signatures verify, but all keys share one AWS account, one region, and one provider control plane. This is neither threshold signing nor decentralized custody.
Real secp256k1 FROST primitives and local composition exist; independent operators, authenticated DKG transport, custody, recovery, and release ceremonies are not evidenced.
Coordinator state, exclusions, blame, and aggregation paths exist, but no distributed participant transport or independently controlled signer fleet is evidenced.
Key aggregation, nonce generation, partial signing, and aggregation wrappers exist without a qualified multi-party session, durable nonce lifecycle, or release integration.
BLS12-381 blinding and DLEQ primitives exist; a live guardian federation, consensus, share custody, database recovery, and end-to-end issuance are absent.
Typed operator and transfer models exist, while value-bearing DKG, signing, rotation, recovery, and operator deployment remain gated.
Provider boundaries and policy are documented, but no independently controlled HSM, Keystone, StrongBox, Secure Enclave, Nitro, or PKCS#11 signer set has complete runtime and release evidence.
